stem: Which sentence states a difference between the two warblers' migration routes?
stimulus:
Notes about two songbirds:
• The blackpoll warbler and the yellow warbler are both small songbirds that nest in North America.
• Each fall, the blackpoll warbler flies up to 2,500 kilometers nonstop over the Atlantic Ocean.
• Each fall, the yellow warbler travels south mostly over land and stops often to feed.
choices: The blackpoll warbler and the yellow warbler are both small songbirds that nest in North America.
The blackpoll warbler flies nonstop over the Atlantic Ocean, whereas the yellow warbler travels mostly over land.
The blackpoll warbler flies up to 2,500 kilometers nonstop over the open Atlantic Ocean each fall.
The yellow warbler flies nonstop over the Atlantic Ocean, whereas the blackpoll warbler travels mostly over land.
explanation: You were asked for a difference in migration routes. Only B names both birds, gives each bird's route, and links them with 'whereas', which marks a contrast. This is the basic move in Rhetorical Synthesis questions whose goal says 'emphasize a difference': both items, the same attribute, and a word that signals contrast.

A.why: You picked a sentence that names both birds, but it states something they share. The task asked how they differ.

C.why: You picked a sentence about one bird only. A difference needs both birds. This sentence never mentions the yellow warbler, so it cannot show a contrast.

D.why: The structure is right, but the facts are swapped. The notes say the blackpoll warbler crosses the ocean and the yellow warbler travels over land. Check which fact belongs to which item.

stem: Which sentence states a difference between the two towns' unemployment rates?
stimulus:
Notes about two towns:
• In 2023, economists studied the labor markets of two towns, Ardell and Brookmere.
• Ardell's unemployment rate was 3 percent.
• Brookmere's unemployment rate was 7 percent.
• The average hourly wage was $22 in both towns.
choices: Ardell and Brookmere had the same average hourly wage in 2023, which was $22.
In 2023, Ardell's unemployment rate was 3 percent, while Brookmere's was 7 percent.
In 2023, economists studied the labor markets of two towns, Ardell and Brookmere.
In 2023, Ardell's unemployment rate was 7 percent, while Brookmere's was 3 percent.
explanation: The task limits you to one attribute, unemployment. B gives both towns' rates side by side and joins them with 'while', so the difference is clear. Some real Rhetorical Synthesis goals narrow the comparison to one feature. Find that feature first, then look for the choice that compares both items on it.

A.why: You compared the towns on the wrong attribute. Wages are not unemployment, and this sentence describes a similarity, not a difference.

C.why: You picked the sentence that names both towns and stopped there. It never says how they differ, so it does not do the job.

D.why: You swapped the numbers. The notes give Ardell 3 percent and Brookmere 7 percent. Match each value to its item before you choose.

stem: Which sentence states a difference in where the verb usually goes in English and in Japanese?
stimulus:
Notes about two languages:
• English and Japanese are each spoken by more than 100 million people.
• In English, the verb usually comes before the object, as in "I read books."
• In Japanese, the verb usually comes at the end of the sentence, after the object.
choices: English and Japanese are each spoken by more than 100 million people around the world.
In English the verb usually comes before the object, but in Japanese it usually comes last.
In Japanese, the verb usually comes at the end of the sentence, after the object.
In English the verb usually comes before the object, and similarly in Japanese it comes last.
explanation: B names both languages, gives each one's verb position, and uses 'but' to mark the contrast. On a real 'emphasize a difference' question, the relation word does as much work as the facts.

A.why: You picked a fact the two languages share. The task asked about word order and a difference, and this sentence gives neither.

C.why: You picked a sentence that describes only Japanese. Without English, there is nothing to contrast with.

D.why: The facts are right, but 'similarly' tells the reader the two languages match, and they don't. The relationship is contrast, so the sentence needs a word like 'but' or 'whereas'.

stem: Which sentence states a difference in how fast the two types of seismic waves travel?
stimulus:
Notes about seismic waves:
• Earthquakes produce two main types of seismic waves, P-waves and S-waves.
• In Earth's crust, P-waves travel about 6 kilometers per second.
• In Earth's crust, S-waves travel about 3.5 kilometers per second.
• P-waves can pass through solids and liquids; S-waves can pass only through solids.
choices: Earthquakes produce two main types of seismic waves, known as P-waves and S-waves.
Unlike P-waves, which pass through solids and liquids, S-waves pass only through solids.
In the crust, P-waves travel about 6 kilometers per second, faster than S-waves at 3.5.
P-waves always travel about twice as fast as S-waves at every depth inside Earth.
explanation: The task restricts you to speed. C gives both waves' speeds in the crust and uses the comparative 'faster than' to connect them. When a real question narrows the goal to one feature, the right choice compares both items on that feature and no other.

A.why: You picked the sentence that lists both waves. It names them but never says how they differ, which is the trap built into comparison questions.

B.why: This sentence does contrast the two waves, but on what they can pass through. The task asked about speed. A real contrast on the wrong attribute still misses the goal.

D.why: The notes give speeds only for the crust, and 6 is not twice 3.5. 'Always' and 'at every depth' claim more than the notes support.

stem: Goal: emphasize a difference in length between the blue whale and the whale shark. Which sentence best does that?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The blue whale and the whale shark both feed on plankton, tiny organisms that drift in the ocean.
• The blue whale is a mammal that breathes air through a blowhole.
• The whale shark is a fish that breathes through gills.
• Adult blue whales can reach about 30 meters in length.
• Adult whale sharks can reach about 18 meters in length.
choices: The blue whale is a mammal that breathes air, whereas the whale shark is a fish that breathes through gills.
Adult blue whales can reach about 30 meters in length, whereas adult whale sharks reach about 18 meters.
Two large ocean animals that feed on plankton are the blue whale and the whale shark.
Adult whale sharks can reach about 30 meters in length, whereas adult blue whales reach about 18 meters.
explanation: The goal limits you to one attribute: length. B names both animals, gives each one's length, and joins them with 'whereas', so the reader sees the difference. This is the first step in every 'emphasize a difference' or 'compare' Rhetorical Synthesis question: find the attribute the goal names, then pick the choice that puts both items' values for that attribute side by side with a word that marks the relationship.

A.why: You saw 'whereas' and two animals and stopped checking. This sentence does contrast the two, but by how they breathe, not by length. The goal named length, so a contrast on any other attribute doesn't do the job.

C.why: You picked a sentence because it mentions both animals. It only lists them and points to something they share. It never says how they differ, and it never mentions length at all.

D.why: You matched the right shape (both animals, both lengths, 'whereas') but didn't check the numbers against the notes. This sentence swaps them. The notes give the blue whale about 30 meters and the whale shark about 18.
